test_case_title: English: Unpaid 2-Month Salary (₹1,80,000), Relieving Letter Hostage & ₹2 Lakh Bond Threat
raw_user_input: I worked as a software developer in Pune and served my full 60-day notice period after sending my resignation email. I have my offer letter, last 3 payslips, and IT laptop handover clearance. However, HR has withheld my last 2 months' salary totaling Rs 180000 and refuses to issue my relieving letter, claiming I violated a 2 lakh training bond by interviewing with a rival company.

decoded_flags.statutory_reality: Under Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, any agreement restraining an employee from exercising a lawful profession after leaving employment is 100% VOID and unenforceable in India (affirmed repeatedly by the Supreme Court).
decoded_flags.recommended_counter_move: Reply calmly that post-termination restraint of trade is void ab initio under Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872.

decoded_flags.clause_or_threat_type: Employment Bond Penalty / Relieving Letter Hostage
decoded_flags.statutory_reality: Under Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, an employer cannot enforce a fixed penalty bond unless they prove actual itemized money spent on specialized external training—and they cannot legally hold a Relieving Letter hostage as coercion.
decoded_flags.recommended_counter_move: Demand an itemized receipt of actual external training expenditure under Section 74 ICA and file a conciliation claim on samadhan.labour.gov.in.

# REGISTERED A.D. / EMAIL — LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE
**WITHOUT PREJUDICE**  
**Strategy Posture:** gemini-2.5-flash (Balanced Legal Strategy)

**Date:** 11 November 2026  
**From:** Aarav Verma (Test Claimant), residing at Flat 402, Indiranagar, Bengaluru - 560038  
**To:** Opposite Party / Respondent, having address at Registered Address of Opposite Party  

**SUBJECT: WITHOUT PREJUDICE — PRE-MEDIATION SETTLEMENT & DEMAND NOTICE FOR ₹180,000 (UNPAID SALARY, DELAYED FULL & FINAL (F&F) SETTLEMENT & WITHHELD RELIEVING LETTER)**

Sir / Madam,

Under instructions from and on behalf of my self-represented claim, I hereby serve upon you the following categorical Legal Demand Notice:

### 1. CHRONOLOGICAL STATEMENT OF FACTS
1. Performed duties under valid employment terms; salary/F&F accrued. (*Establishes statutory wage liability under Payment of Wages Act Sec 3 & Sec 5.*)
2. Completed handover / served notice period or terminated by employer. (*Triggers statutory deadline for Full & Final settlement and service certificate release.*)
3. Employer withholding ₹180,000 unpaid wages/F&F or holding Relieving Letter hostage.

### 2. APPLICABLE STATUTORY PROVISIONS (VERIFIED INDIAN LAW)
Your continued failure and refusal to discharge the lawful liability of **₹180,000** is in direct breach of the following statutory provisions:
- **Payment of Wages Act, 1936 (Section 3, Section 5 & Section 15):** Mandates strict timelines for payment of earned wages upon work completion or termination, and empowers the Authority under Section 15(3) to direct refund of unlawful deductions along with compensation.
- **Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (Section 2(s), Section 25F & Section 33C(2)):** Any workman (non-managerial employee) entitled to money or benefit capable of being computed in terms of money from the employer may apply to the Labour Court for recovery.
- **Indian Contract Act, 1872 (Section 27):** Every agreement by which anyone is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind is to that extent void. Post-termination non-compete threats blocking an employee from joining another company are legally unenforceable.
- **Indian Contract Act, 1872 (Section 74 (Employment Bond Penalty Limit)):** Employers cannot enforce extortionate 'employment bond' penalties or hold relieving/experience letters hostage unless they prove actual, itemized financial expenditure spent on specialized external training.
- **State Shops and Commercial Establishments Act (Provisions on Notice Pay & Final Settlement):** Covers white-collar IT, startup, and office employees; empowers the local Labour Officer / Inspector to summon employers withholding earned salary, leave encashment, or service certificates.

### 3. FINAL DEMAND & CONSEQUENCE OF NON-COMPLIANCE
I hereby call upon you to:
1. Remit the principal sum of **₹180,000** (Rupees 180,000 only) along with accrued interest @ 18% per annum immediately via NEFT/IMPS/UPI; and
2. Issue written confirmation of compliance within **5 (five) days** from the receipt of this Notice.

In the spirit of amicable resolution, if the principal sum of **₹180,000** is remitted within **5 (five) days**, I undertake to waive accrued interest and close the matter with a formal No-Dues receipt, failing which the claim will be referred to **https://samadhan.labour.gov.in (SAMADHAN — Software Application for Monitoring and Disposal, Handling of Industrial Disputes)**.

A copy of this Notice is retained in my records for production before the competent Court/Authority as Annexures.

Yours faithfully,

**Aarav Verma (Test Claimant)**  
*(Claimant)*
